# CANDIDATE: OPENING_RANGE_VOLUME_IMBALANCE_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-08-20  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The opening range volume imbalance (ORVI) predicts the directional bias of the SPY for the remainder of the trading session. A significant imbalance favoring buying pressure (high ORVI) indicates a bullish bias, while an imbalance favoring selling pressure (low ORVI) indicates a bearish bias. We hypothesize that trading in the direction of the ORVI signal (using 0DTE options) will capture edge on the J anchor days, particularly the bearish winner days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04) where we expect a negative ORVI (selling pressure) to trigger PUT trades.

## Mechanism

At the open (09:30 ET), we calculate the volume imbalance over the first 15 minutes (or until 10:00 ET) as: ORVI = (buy_volume - sell_volume) / (buy_volume + sell_volume), where buy_volume is volume on upticks and sell_volume on downticks (or using the trade sign from the OPRA data). If ORVI < -0.2 (indicating strong selling pressure), we enter a bearish trade (SPY 0DTE PUT at ATM or 1st OTM strike). If ORVI > 0.2 (strong buying pressure), we enter a bullish trade (CALL). Otherwise, no trade. Entry is at the open of the 15-minute bar following the signal bar (or at the close of the signal bar, depending on data availability). Exit follows the BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON rules for PUTs and BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON for CALLs, including chart-stop primary, chandelier profit-lock, and premium stop as catastrophe cap.
